# [CS001] SQL Injection (sql-injection)

A SQL statement is built from untrusted data.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html) |
| **OWASP** | A05:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Concatenating or formatting request data into a query lets the client change the statement's structure: read other rows, bypass a WHERE clause or run additional statements. database/sql, sqlx, pgx and gorm all accept placeholders whose values the driver sends separately from the SQL text, so the input can never become syntax. The taint engine follows the data across functions, closures and struct fields and shows the path.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func user(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.URL.Query().Get("id")
	row := db.QueryRowContext(r.Context(), "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = "+id)
	_ = row.Scan(&name)
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func user(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.URL.Query().Get("id")
	row := db.QueryRowContext(r.Context(), "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = $1", id)
	_ = row.Scan(&name)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [sql-injection]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    sql-injection: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore sql-injection -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** sql-injection
```
